title: Derived tensor product of etale sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $T$ a scheme, and work on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $\Lambda_T$ be the constant sheaf of rings [def-kun-constant-sheaf], and use the derived category $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Complexes are cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]; acyclic means all cohomology sheaves vanish [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], and a quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

For complexes $\mathcal E^\bullet,\mathcal F^\bullet$, the notation $\mathcal E^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F^\bullet$ means the direct-sum total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] on the ringed site $(T_{\Et},\Lambda_T)$: its degree $n$ term is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\mathcal E^p\otimes_{\Lambda_T}\mathcal F^q$ and its differential on the $(p,q)$ summand is $d_{\mathcal E}\otimes 1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_{\mathcal F}$.

A complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ of $\Lambda_T$-modules is *K-flat* if $\mathcal E^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F^\bullet$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$. This is the ringed-site K-flat notion [def-pc-kflat-complex], with the tensor factors interchanged by the sign symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ in bidegree $(p,q)$.

For $K_1,K_2\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ choose representing complexes $C_1^\bullet,C_2^\bullet$, and a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to C_1^\bullet$ with $P^\bullet$ K-flat (such resolutions are supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on $(T_{\Et},\Lambda_T)$). The *derived tensor product* is represented by the total tensor complex:

$$
K_1\kunotimes{\Lambda}K_2
=Q\bigl(P^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda C_2^\bullet\bigr)
\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda),
$$

where $Q$ is the localization functor of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Independence of the chosen K-flat model is recorded with the other properties of this construction. For $K\in D(T_{\Et})$ (integer coefficients) and a complex of $\mathbf Z$-modules $\mathcal M^\bullet$, $K\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\underline{\mathcal M^\bullet}$ denotes derived tensor with the termwise constant complex of [def-kun-constant-sheaf].

lean.statement:
noncomputable def derivedTensor :
    DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A)
lean.note: Specialize A to ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ for Λ : Type (u + 1), [CommRing Λ], and X to T : Scheme.{u}. The result is a bifunctor on exactly Etale.DerivedCategoryModule Λ T, the encoding recorded by def-weil-pbc-derived-categories. This is the existing unbounded K-flat-derived tensor, not the degreewise Tor functor. Ordinary tensor of complexes is HomologicalComplex.tensorObj, defined as mapBifunctor with curriedTensor; ComplexShape.up ℤ gives direct-sum totalization with second differential sign (-1)^p and symmetry (-1)^(pq). DerivedCategory.tensorLeftCounit and isIso_tensorLeftCounit identify the value on Q(P), Q(C₂) with Q(P tensor C₂) for K-flat P; a quasi-isomorphism P → C₁ identifies Q(P) with K₁. The acyclic-test and quasi-isomorphism-preservation definitions of K-flat agree by the mapping-cone criterion and signed symmetry, without boundedness or termwise flatness assumptions. For integer coefficients use ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ), equivalent to AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} by restriction along ULift.ringEquiv.symm followed by the integer-module forget₂ and the termwise constant complex from def-kun-constant-sheaf. No duplicate derived-tensor construction is introduced.
